title: Compatible finite polynomial maps with unit-denominator presentations
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $P,Q$ be commutative $k$-algebras essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, and let $u:P\twoheadrightarrow A$, $v:Q\twoheadrightarrow A$ be surjective $k$-algebra homomorphisms. There exist integers $r,s\geq0$, elements $p_1,\ldots,p_r\in P$, $q_1,\ldots,q_s\in Q$, elements $\widetilde q_1,\ldots,\widetilde q_s\in P$, $\widetilde p_1,\ldots,\widetilde p_r\in Q$, and $k$-algebra maps $f:D\to P$, $g:D\to Q$ from the finite polynomial algebra $D=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with $f(x_i)=p_i$, $f(y_j)=\widetilde q_j$, $g(x_i)=\widetilde p_i$, $g(y_j)=q_j$, $u(\widetilde q_j)=v(q_j)$, and $v(\widetilde p_i)=u(p_i)$. Their composites agree: $u\circ f=v\circ g=:h$. Every $p\in P$ admits $a,t\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\subseteq D$ such that $f(t)$ is a unit and $p f(t)=f(a)$. Every $q\in Q$ admits $c,z\in k[y_1,\ldots,y_s]\subseteq D$ such that $g(z)$ is a unit and $q g(z)=g(c)$. No locality or regularity of $P,Q,A$ is assumed; the sequences of variables may be empty.

source.place: Tag 00SF (lemma-lci-local), polynomial-local presentation comparison; agent refinement using simultaneous finite generators and lifts, abstracted from returned proof steps 1, 2 and the fraction descriptions in step 4.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], choose $k$-algebras $B,C$ of finite type, multiplicative subsets $W\subseteq B$, $V\subseteq C$, and $k$-algebra isomorphisms $\theta:W^{-1}B\to P$, $\eta:V^{-1}C\to Q$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], choose surjective $k$-algebra maps $e:k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\to B$ and $d:k[y_1,\ldots,y_s]\to C$. Write $b_i=e(x_i)$, $c_j=d(y_j)$, and set $p_i=\theta(b_i/1)$, $q_j=\eta(c_j/1)$. These choices allow $r=0$ or $s=0$.

Surjectivity of $u$ gives a lift $\widetilde q_j\in P$ with $u(\widetilde q_j)=v(q_j)$ for each $j$; surjectivity of $v$ gives $\widetilde p_i\in Q$ with $v(\widetilde p_i)=u(p_i)$ for each $i$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] defines $f,g$ on $D=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s]$ by the stipulated variable images. The composites $uf,vg$ agree on each $x_i$ and $y_j$, hence are equal by uniqueness in that same universal property; call the common map $h$. The inclusions of the two polynomial blocks into $D$ extend each monomial by exponent zero on the other block; distinct monomials remain distinct, so both inclusions are injective.

source.place: Tag 00SF (lemma-lci-local), polynomial-presentation comparison; agent construction using the polynomial universal property.

proof.text: For $p\in P$, represent $\theta^{-1}(p)=b/w$ with $b\in B$ and $w\in W$, using the fraction definition in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Choose $a,t\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ with $e(a)=b$ and $e(t)=w$ by surjectivity of $e$. On this block, $f=\theta\circ(b\mapsto b/1)\circ e$, since these maps agree on variables by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Thus $f(t)=\theta(w/1)$ is a unit with inverse $\theta(1/w)$, and $p f(t)=\theta((b/w)(w/1))=\theta(b/1)=f(a)$. The fraction identities follow directly from multiplication and equality of fractions: $(w/1)(1/w)=1$ and $(b/w)(w/1)=b/1$.

For $q\in Q$, write $\eta^{-1}(q)=c_0/v_0$ with $c_0\in C$, $v_0\in V$. Choose $c,z\in k[y_1,\ldots,y_s]$ with $d(c)=c_0$, $d(z)=v_0$. On this block $g=\eta\circ(c_0\mapsto c_0/1)\circ d$ by uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Hence $g(z)=\eta(v_0/1)$ has inverse $\eta(1/v_0)$ and $qg(z)=\eta((c_0/v_0)(v_0/1))=\eta(c_0/1)=g(c)$, using the fraction definition in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. All arguments hold for empty blocks (whose polynomial algebra is $k$) and for the zero ring, where $0=1$ is a unit. They use no locality or regularity assumption.
